acceptedAnswer.text: Gum contouring is carried out under local anaesthetic, so the procedure itself should not be painful. After the anaesthetic wears off, some tenderness and mild discomfort are common for a few days. Most patients find this manageable with over-the-counter pain relief. Laser-assisted techniques may reduce post-operative discomfort compared to traditional surgical methods, though individual experiences vary. Your dentist will discuss pain management options with you before and after the procedure to ensure you feel as comfortable as possible throughout.

mainEntity.name: How long do the results of gum contouring last?

acceptedAnswer.text: When performed correctly and supported by good oral health, the results of gum contouring are generally long-lasting. The removed gum tissue does not typically grow back. However, factors such as ongoing gum disease, medication-related gum changes, or poor oral hygiene may affect the long-term appearance of the gum line. Maintaining regular dental visits and a thorough home care routine helps to preserve the results. Your dentist will advise on any specific aftercare steps relevant to your individual situation.

mainEntity.name: Can gum contouring fix uneven gums?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gum contouring can be an effective approach for addressing an uneven gum line, where some teeth appear longer or shorter than others due to inconsistent gum tissue levels. By carefully reshaping the tissue, a dentist can create a more symmetrical and proportionate gum line. However, the suitability and extent of correction depend on the underlying anatomy, including the position of the bone and the health of the gum tissue. A clinical assessment will help determine what level of improvement may be achievable.

mainEntity.name: Are there risks associated with gum contouring?

acceptedAnswer.text: As with any dental or surgical procedure, gum contouring carries some risks. These may include infection, prolonged sensitivity, bleeding, or an uneven result. In rare cases, damage to the tooth root or surrounding structures may occur. Choosing a qualified and experienced dental professional helps to minimise these risks. Your dentist will explain the potential risks and benefits during your consultation, allowing you to make an informed decision about whether to proceed with treatment.

mainEntity.name: How much does gum contouring cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of gum contouring in the UK varies depending on the complexity of the case, the number of teeth involved, and the technique used. As a cosmetic procedure, gum contouring is not typically available on the NHS and is usually provided privately. During your consultation, your dentist will provide a personalised treatment plan that includes clear information about fees. It is advisable to discuss costs, payment options, and what the treatment fee covers before committing to any procedure.

mainEntity.name: Can I have gum contouring if I have gum disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: Active gum disease would generally need to be treated and stabilised before any cosmetic gum procedure could be considered. Gum contouring performed on unhealthy tissue may lead to complications, delayed healing, or unsatisfactory results. Your dentist will assess the health of your gums thoroughly and, if necessary, recommend a course of periodontal treatment before discussing cosmetic options. Addressing gum disease first supports both your oral health and the likelihood of a successful cosmetic outcome.
